judge_output.rationale: The claim that partial Dyson-sphere waste heat (100-1000 K) appears as a photospheric infrared excess in very few stars has been tested on Gaia+2MASS+WISE photometry, yielding occurrence upper limits near 1 in 10^5 (2022MNRAS.512.2988S) and a handful of M-dwarf candidates (2024MNRAS.531..695S). Those candidates are now largely attributed to background contamination (2024RNAAS...8..145R, 2026arXiv260703619R). A data-driven W1/W2 excess search over five million FGK stars (2024AJ....168..157C) covers the same 3-5 um band but only with two broadband points. None of the listed works uses SPHEREx channel-resolved 3-5 um spectra to test whether the residual is a smooth, featureless single-temperature 300-600 K blackbody, so the card is a new-archive, sharper-observable version of an already tested claim.

closest_prior.relation: Fit photosphere-plus-blackbody SEDs to Gaia DR3/2MASS/AllWISE photometry for ~5 million stars and found 7 M-dwarf excess candidates; it used broadband WISE points rather than SPHEREx spectra and placed no limit on spectral smoothness.

Set upper limits of order 1 in 10^5 on the fraction of stars hosting 100-1000 K partial Dyson spheres, using Gaia DR2+AllWISE colour cuts; same occurrence-rate claim, but with colours and no spectral-shape test.

Searched 4.9 million main-sequence FGK stars for W1/W2 (3.4/4.6 um) excess with machine-learning photospheric predictions and found 53 objects; same wavelength range, but only two broadband points and no blackbody-temperature or feature-depth test.
Fit 100-600 K blackbodies to IRAS LRS spectra of ~250,000 sources and set Dyson-sphere upper limits; spectral-shape test of the same claim, but at longer wavelengths and much shallower depth.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work uses SPHEREx 3.0-5.0 um channel-resolved residuals over a Gaia XP+2MASS photosphere to bound the fraction of 100-pc dwarfs with a >5 per cent excess that is a featureless single 300-600 K blackbody, so delivering that per-channel spectral-shape constraint and ranked residue table is the new contribution.
